pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/engine/src/invocation/run.rs:106 The one spawn door gives every killed child the same retryable Timeout whatever its Mode, so an Edit run whose side effects may have escaped is closed as an ordinary failure instead of an indeterminate outcome, and its consumers re-run it (relay retries) or commit its partial edits (responder ACT).

techniques.evidence: crates/engine/src/invocation/run.rs:168 The kill path has no Mode input and the error vocabulary has no unknown-outcome status. A killed Generate run is close to a pure read; a killed Edit run is the side-effecting case the technique names. Consumers confirm the harm: crates/agent/src/exec.rs:133 settles it failed (re-run up to max_attempts per docs/RELAY.md), and crates/responder/src/act.rs:95-101 commits whatever the killed run left.

crates/engine/src/invocation/posture.rs:124 Read-only is judged only over the argv allowlist, yet a non-bare scan runs in the workspace, and posture.rs:165 itself says CLAUDE.md, hooks or settings in a cwd are inherited. No setting-sources pin exists (repo grep: zero hits) and --bare requires an API key, so a seat scan cannot use it. Those policy inputs sit in a tree that committers and earlier Edit runs can write, and the writer set is not recorded beside the guard. How far project settings widen the allowlist is CLI behaviour I did not run. The Codex path does hold custody: --ignore-user-config, --ignore-rules, neutral cwd, and a fail-closed audit.

crates/engine/src/invocation/posture.rs:198 The launch door removes only the billing key; no prefix scrub exists (repo grep for CLAUDECODE|CLAUDE_CODE: zero hits; no env_clear in these dirs). A process launched from a Claude Code session carries CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN and CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS (names observed in this session), and .claude/skills/gateway-onboard runs lt-runner from such a session. Daemon launchers are unaffected. The technique reports the environment half as harmless on one CLI; actual harm here is unmeasured.
crates/engine/src/invocation/posture.rs:189 The only environment-read capability is a credential, which the technique classes as a legitimate runtime fact; there is no client-surface capability here.

crates/engine/src/codex/resolve.rs:24 Narrow finding: the only code-naming input in this seam is the child binary, set from startup env, CLI or local config (responder config.rs:93, runner main.rs:64, agent config.rs:46); crates/api has no claude_bin or codex_bin. The seam loads no in-process extensions, so the required-flag and isolation-wrapper rules have nothing to bind.
crates/engine/src/invocation/tools.rs:54 What is composed is a flat argv with no hook chain, so there is no assembly for a digest to identify; the seam computes no digest.
crates/engine/src/codex/posture.rs:49 The seam composes no hook chain of its own; the Codex path turns the child's hooks off, and any Claude child hooks run inside the foreign CLI.

crates/engine/src/codex/posture.rs:42 This seam performs no extension install or registration write; on the Codex path the plugin surface is disabled. Technique read through its opening sections only.
crates/engine/src/invocation/run.rs:133 Input is one-shot: stdin closes after the prompt, so the seam has no mid-run input door.
crates/engine/src/sandbox/contree.rs:96 Sandbox work is a blocking call bounded by a wall clock; no remote handle is held across model turns.
crates/engine/src/invocation/mod.rs:72 Each invocation is a single call with no durable conversation state; grep for checkpoint and resume across invocation, codex and sandbox found nothing.

pairs.registryProposal: The subject is framed around an in-process runtime, but a seam that launches a foreign agent CLI still has to meet guard-input-custody, nested-run-is-not-its-parent and indeterminate-closure-on-interruption while most other techniques have no surface. Name this launcher topology in the golden path's scope section, and say whether indeterminate closure binds a supervisor that kills a side-effecting child itself, since the technique is written around restart recovery.
